brand.name: Mile Zero
brand.tagline: Business and finance, from the starting line.

stages.label: Mile 0
stages.name: Briefing Check
stages.summary: A short check that your team has read the Opening Case. Five or six auto-marked questions, ten minutes once opened. Not scored: it just makes sure nobody starts behind.
submit: One set of answers per team

stages.label: Mile 1
stages.name: Where to Play
stages.summary: Market data, customer interviews and a survey. Decide which markets to enter first, which to leave for later, and which to walk away from.

stages.label: Mile 2
stages.name: Making It Pay
stages.summary: Choose how the company makes money, build a three-year plan inside the budget, and test what happens if sales come in slower than hoped.

stages.label: Nominations
stages.name: School nominations
stages.summary: Each school nominates one team to continue, based on Mile 1 and Mile 2.

stages.label: Mile 3
stages.name: Project Kestrel
stages.summary: Something unexpected lands on the CEO's desk. Decide whether to accept, reject or negotiate, and show what changes in your plan.

stages.label: Live Final
stages.name: Live Final
stages.summary: Present your strategy in up to seven minutes, take five minutes of judges' questions, then respond live to new information you haven't seen before.

criteria.name: Problem framing
criteria.question: Did you find the central problem and build a clear strategy around it?

criteria.name: Evidence and analysis
criteria.question: Is the evidence relevant, read correctly and used to support your recommendation?

criteria.name: Feasibility and numbers
criteria.question: Could the company actually do this, and do the numbers add up?

criteria.name: Recommendation and trade-offs
criteria.question: Did you make a clear call and admit the main risks and alternatives?

criteria.name: Communication
criteria.question: Is it clear, concise and persuasive?
